A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

TPA enhances cell survival by inducing radial spreading, which is a form of spreading that is independent of serum, whereas TPA inhibits cell growth by inhibiting the polarized spreading of cells that is dependent on serum.

TPA enhances the survival of cells in contact with the substratum by promoting radial spreading, and inhibits cell growth by preventing cells from spreading and from forming stress fibers and focal contacts.
TPA-induced cell survival is mediated through radial spreading, which is caused by the inhibition of polarized adhesion.

the effect of the phorbol esters on spreading behavior may be a key to understanding their tumor-promoting activity.
